source.title: Belfast News-Letter, 6 June 1958, p. 5 ("Rural councils: results of polling")
source.publisher: Belfast News-Letter (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)

note: Triennial election of the rural district councillors, polled Thursday 5 June 1958. Two contests, Claudy and Middle Liberties (Belfast News-Letter, 6 June 1958, p. 5; Irish News, 6 June 1958, p. 1). The eleven unopposed members added from the Derry Journal, 23 May 1958, p. 7, which names each with the division (Upper Liberties printed as his townland) (round-2 gap-fill, 7 Nov 2026). Coyle was the outgoing Nationalist member.
correctionNote: Renamed from 'Middle Liberties' to Liberties Middle (13 Nov 2026, by the owner's rule for division spellings: the official or DED-map name where there is one, otherwise the spelling most rounds use): the DED maps of 1930-69 (LIBERTIES MIDDLE) spell it Liberties Middle. This round was filed under the spelling 'Middle Liberties', a form of the division's name it keeps as an alias; the old address (middle-liberties) answers with a redirect to this one.
